One Man, One Untouched Ballot

Overnight, a party court did what no pollster managed. It benched half of Netanyahu's own MPs. In one ruling.

Likud's internal tribunal reversed a decision its own Central Committee had approved just last week. Sitting ministers, MKs, and former lawmakers can no longer run in the party's reserved regional slots. Only newcomers can.

Judges explained why those slots exist. They called them "a protected space that has enabled new leadership to sprout in fair conditions… and that started the careers of most [current] Likud ministers". The door that built their careers just got locked from the inside. Nobody in the room objected out loud.

The tribunal also found real problems with last week's vote. Observers were missing for hours. Ballots, envelopes, and voter counts didn't match at several stations. The panel ruled: "The flaws identified in the voting process do not allow the decision to stand". Too broken to certify. Not broken enough, apparently, to order a recount or a new vote — the court cited the tight clock before the August 17 primary.

One ballot came through the audit spotless. Netanyahu's own. Judges found "no supporting evidence" it was fraudulently recorded, ruling the polling protocol showed "orderly documentation of his vote". His eight personally reserved list slots survived intact, too.

MKs hoping to run in slots reserved for women or minorities face their own toll. They must resign from the Knesset before the primary and give up state campaign funding to compete.

Likud currently holds 43 Knesset seats through Norwegian Law rotations. More than half of those officials already had shaky prospects on the new list before this ruling. One earlier estimate put as much as 70 percent of Likud's sitting ministers and MKs at risk of never seeing the next Knesset.
